findings.clause: he must notice, weigh, and speak aloud about
findings.quote: I said to Bruno that I wasn t sure which way was back, and that was scary because he was trusting me, and I couldn t let him down, so we just-we just kept going forward because stopping didn t help.
findings.claim: In his retelling he does not verbalise that he recognised Bruno s pressing as the warning.
findings.fix: none applied - see the arbitration in notes

iterations.notes: R5 still established on all three limbs after the shortening. R1 undisturbed. R3 not engaged by the gift of a stone. One medium R2 finding, OVERRULED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR and recorded rather than acted on: R2 governs what [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] must do ON THE HILL when Bruno warns him, and he did it there - he stopped and spoke aloud to the dog, and that chapter scored 10 on this same rule. This chapter is him RETELLING the event to his parents days later. A rule about conduct does not also require the conduct to be re-enacted inside a later report of it, and reading it that way would make every summary of a past scene a fresh breach. The score is left as the critic returned it because it does not change the verdict.
